title: Parsers
blurb: Verdicts, answers, scores and answer comparison.

blocks.name: slmjury.parsers.judgement
blocks.lead: Verdict parsing (Correct/Incorrect) for SLM judge responses.

about.html: Extractors run in priority order (boxed, markdown bold, labeled, quick verdict, sentence patterns, then a fallback), and each has a confidence level.

blocks.name: ParseResult
blocks.sig: (verdict: str, confidence: str, method: str, raw_match: Optional[str]) -> None
blocks.summary: Result of parsing a judge response.

blocks.name: parse_judgement
blocks.summary: Parse a judge response into "Correct", "Incorrect" or "Undefined".

blocks.name: parse_judgement_detailed
blocks.summary: Parse a judge response; returns a ParseResult with verdict, confidence, method and raw match.

body.html: Tries, in order: \boxed{} and bold (high confidence), labels like "VERDICT: X", a standalone verdict word at the start and sentences like "The answer is X" (medium), then the last verdict word (low).

blocks.name: get_verdict_confidence
blocks.summary: The verdict and its confidence level as a tuple (legacy interface).

blocks.name: parse_batch
blocks.summary: Parse a list of judge responses into ParseResult objects.

blocks.name: get_parsing_stats
blocks.summary: Counts and rates by verdict, confidence and method over a batch of ParseResult objects.

blocks.name: slmjury.parsers.answer
blocks.lead: Answer extraction from model responses across dataset types.

about.html: Handles numeric (GSM8K, GSM-Plus), LaTeX (MATH) and multiple-choice (ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge) answers, and edge cases such as repetitive outputs, malformed delimiters and units.

blocks.name: extract_answer
blocks.summary: Extract the final answer from a model response.

body.html: `dataset_type` is "numeric", "latex" or "multiple_choice". Returns "UNABLE_TO_EXTRACT" when no answer is found.

blocks.name: get_dataset_type
blocks.summary: Map a dataset name (e.g. "gsm8k", "math", "arc_easy") to "numeric", "latex" or "multiple_choice".

blocks.name: slmjury.parsers.normalizer
blocks.lead: Answer normalization and comparison for numeric, LaTeX (MATH) and multiple-choice datasets.

about.html: MATH pairs are looked up in slmjury/parsers/math_labels.json, which scripts/build_math_labels.py builds from the rules in `_strip_format and _compare_latex_raw`; a pair the table lacks is compared live under a time limit.

blocks.name: answers_are_equivalent
blocks.sig: (predicted: str, ground_truth: str, dataset_type: str = 'numeric') -> bool
blocks.summary: Whether `predicted matches ground_truth` for a dataset type ("numeric", "latex" or "multiple_choice").

body.html: An empty answer or UNABLE_TO_EXTRACT never matches.

blocks.name: numbers_are_equivalent
blocks.summary: Legacy alias — use answers_are_equivalent() instead.

blocks.name: normalize_numeric
blocks.summary: Normalize a numeric string for comparison: commas, currency symbols, units, fractions and word multipliers.

blocks.name: MissingLabel
blocks.summary: Strict mode met a pair the label file does not hold.

blocks.name: ComparisonTimeout
blocks.summary: The time limit fired. A BaseException, so no except Exception can swallow it.

blocks.name: set_strict_labels
blocks.summary: In strict mode a pair missing from the label file raises instead of being computed.

blocks.name: label_key
blocks.summary: The label file's key for one stripped (answer, gold) pair.

blocks.name: labels_digest
blocks.summary: SHA-256 of the labels alone, so a rebuild with the same labels keeps its sha.

blocks.name: label_sha
blocks.summary: The loaded label file's sha. Raises when there is no label file.

blocks.name: compare_with_limit
blocks.sig: (pred: str, gold: str, seconds: float = 8) -> Tuple[bool, bool]
blocks.summary: (equivalent, timed_out) from the rules, under a time limit where the platform has one.

blocks.name: slmjury.parsers.score
blocks.lead: Score parsing (1-5) for open-ended SLM judge responses.

about.html: Single scores, MT-Bench style (\boxed{4}), and multi-dimension scores, SummEval style (\boxed{coherence=4, consistency=3, ...}), each through a priority cascade like judgement.py's.

blocks.name: parse_score
blocks.summary: Extract one score from a judge response: an integer in [1, max_score], or None.

body.html: Tries, in order: \boxed{N} or \boxed{N/5}, N or N/5, [[N]], "Score: N" / "Rating: N" / "N out of 5", then the last standalone integer in [1, max_score].

blocks.name: parse_multi_score
blocks.sig: (response: str, dimensions: tuple[str, ...] = ('coherence', 'consistency', 'fluency', 'relevance'), max_score: int = 5) -> dict[str, Optional[int]]
blocks.summary: Extract per-dimension scores from a SummEval-style response; returns {dimension: int or None}.

body.html: Tries, in order: structured boxed (\boxed{coherence=4, ...}, also inside \text{} or $...$), positional boxed (\boxed{3,2,2,3}, in dimension order), per-dimension boxed ("Coherence: \boxed{4}"), then labels ("Coherence: 4").
